Bayesian unfolding

Source: R/svb.R
bunfld.Rd

The lognormal model of bmdsf() for a respondent-by-stimulus matrix: \(\log \delta_{ij} \sim N(\log \lVert x_i - z_j \rVert, 1 / \tau)\), \(N(0, 10^2)\) priors on every coordinate and \(\tau \sim U(0, 10)\) (Bakker and Poole 2013). Feeling thermometers \(T\) on 0-100 enter as \(\delta = (100 - T) / 50\). Given the stimuli the respondents are independent, and the other way round, so each block is slice sampled at once, dimension by dimension; draws are aligned on the stimuli. The chain starts from the singular value decomposition of the centred matrix. Draws come from seed, as set.seed() takes it.

Usage

bunfld(D, ndim = 2, nsamp = 1000, burn = 200, seed = 42)

Arguments

D

A respondent-by-stimulus matrix of dissimilarities.

ndim

The number of dimensions.

nsamp

The draws kept.

burn

The sweeps discarded first.

seed

The seed.

Value

A list of class bunfld: stim (aligned posterior means), sd, ideal, dist (posterior mean respondent-stimulus distances), sigma, tau and nsamp.

References

Bakker, R. and Poole, K. T. (2013). Bayesian metric multidimensional scaling. Political Analysis, 21(1), 125-140. doi:10.1093/pan/mps039

See also

Other scaling: amscal(), anchv(), anomin(), bamscl(), bbscal(), bmdsf(), cjrirt(), cmdsf(), cutlns(), dblctr(), dwnom(), dynirt(), indscl(), ipsrec(), irtem(), irtlik(), irtpst(), mdsfit(), mlsmu(), nmdsf(), nombt(), nomll(), nompr(), nomutl(), nrmvec(), optcls(), ordirt(), ordocl(), procrs(), scboot(), smacf(), smunf(), unfstr(), votagr(), wrdfsh()

Examples

set.seed(1)
S <- matrix(runif(8, -0.5, 0.5), 4)
R <- matrix(runif(60, -0.5, 0.5), 30)
D <- sqrt(outer(R[, 1], S[, 1], "-")^2 + outer(R[, 2], S[, 2], "-")^2)
f <- bunfld(D, nsamp = 50, burn = 50)
cor(as.numeric(f$dist), as.numeric(D))
#> [1] 0.9766247
